sections.title: Fuzzy matching
sections.summary: Index and rank fuzzy matches for titles, IDs and branches.

requirements.text: Build a pure search index from the loaded Trace: one entry per PRD section, spec section or task, retaining its existing Node identity. Index section titles and IDs and task titles and branch names; no server endpoint, persisted index or new contract field is needed.

Trim the query and match case-insensitively. Support ordered subsequences for abbreviations and a single insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent transposition for query tokens of at least four characters; shorter tokens require exact, prefix or subsequence matches. Every whitespace-separated query token must match within one indexed field. Rank exact field matches first, then prefixes, contiguous matches, typo matches and subsequences; within a match class prefer titles, then IDs, then branches, then prose. Break remaining ties by score, source order and stable node key.

Return one result per node with its best matching field, score and sorted, non-overlapping, half-open UTF-16 ranges in the original visible text. Case normalization must preserve a mapping back to source positions and never split a surrogate pair. An empty query returns no search results. The same trace and query always produce the same order.

Cache the index by searchable trace content and rebuild it only when that content changes. Query changes reuse the index; status-only refreshes do not trigger markdown parsing. Keep matching and result derivation pure and use installed Effect core APIs. No search dependency is selected or added by this plan.

tests.text: Results have unique node identities, deterministic order and valid non-overlapping source ranges; normalized matches never split surrogate pairs.
Exact titles outrank fuzzy titles; abbreviations and one-edit typos match; blank and unmatched queries, punctuation and mixed-case Unicode are covered.

sections.title: Search controls and chain highlighting
sections.summary: Add search navigation and temporary chain highlighting.

requirements.text: Add window-local query and active-result state to the Schema-defined Model, with fact-named messages for query edits, result navigation, result selection and clearing. The pure update function derives results and reconciles the active node after trace refresh: retain it if still matched, otherwise choose the first result or none. Query edits reset to the first result; empty and unmatched queries have no active chain.

Render a labelled toolbar search input, result count and ranked result list showing kind, title and matched field. Use accessible combobox/listbox semantics with an active descendant, ArrowUp/ArrowDown navigation bounded at the list ends, Enter to select, pointer selection, and Escape to clear. Handle these keys only in the search control; they must not reach the reader's own keys, such as Escape. Announce the count and no-results state without stealing focus.

Selecting a result brings it into view in the reader. For a PRD section, the PRD pane scrolls to its heading. For a spec section or a task, the first PRD section of its chain, in document order, is the current section for as long as the result is active, ahead of the pin and without changing the pin or the PRD pane's scroll; its card, row and chip scroll into view in their own panes, and a result in a spec section's prose shows that card open while it is active. A spec section that implements no PRD section has no card to go to: selecting it opens it in the detail panel, the one case where a result opens the panel. Keep keyboard focus in search. Preview its chain as a hover does. Only the active result contributes a search chain; never union separate result chains into a synthetic chain.

Mark direct text matches with semantic mark nodes and a separate node outline, in PRD headings and prose, spec card headers, summaries and full sections, task rows and chips; related chain members get chain highlighting but no text marks unless they independently match. Hover remains the top preview, above search. Draw a curve as part of a chain only when both endpoints belong to that same chain. Use text labels or outlines as well as colour to identify the active result.

Clearing search removes its marks, outline, results and temporary chain while preserving the pinned section, the detail panel, document content and task state. The current section goes back to the pin or to the section at the top. A no-results query shows a message without dimming the panes. Pinning a section and opening a task continue to work. Keep the existing markdown lazy boundaries effective when queries change.

tests.text: Type an abbreviation or typo, navigate with arrows, select with Enter and pointer, and assert matching text, active result and connected-chain highlighting.
Search, hover and a pinned section coexist; clearing and Escape preserve the pin and the detail panel; zero matches leave the panes usable; refreshed and removed results reconcile correctly.

Select a spec section and a task whose PRD section is not the pinned one: its PRD section is current while the result is active and the pin comes back when the search is cleared; unrelated curves stay unlit. Select spec.format, which implements no PRD section, and find it open in the detail panel.

sections.title: Prose search and inline highlights
sections.summary: Search markdown prose with snippets and inline match highlights.

requirements.text: Extend the index to visible PRD and spec prose, owned by the nearest preceding section heading until the next heading of any level; nested sections own their text and do not duplicate it in their parent. Extract paragraphs, list items, table cells, link labels and inline code from the markdown AST. Exclude HTML/comments, heading ID attributes, link destinations, code fences and Mermaid content; diffs and session logs remain out of scope.

Keep a visible-text-to-AST-text-node offset map for each searchable prose block. Match within a paragraph, list paragraph or table cell, including across emphasis, links and inline code, but not across block or section boundaries. Reuse the fuzzy ranking and source ranges from fuzzy-matching; prose ranks below titles within a match class. Return one result per node, with its best match and a bounded context snippet from the matching block.

Render match ranges as semantic mark nodes in snippets and in document text leaves, splitting ranges across existing inline elements while preserving formatting, safe links, text selection and heading IDs. Do not rewrite source markdown, inject HTML or wrap DOM after rendering. Highlight the best matching field or prose block per result consistently with its snippet. For typo matches, mark the matched source word; for subsequences, mark matched characters.

Parse each changed document once and share its AST and position mapping between indexing and rendering. Query edits only rematch and render marks. Reconcile results and offsets when source content changes. Selecting a prose result brings the matched block into view, falling back to the owning section until block measurement is available; keep code highlighting and diagram mounts stable.

tests.text: Highlighting preserves the original visible text and every range maps to text in its owning section.
Find prose spanning bold text and a link, inspect the highlighted snippet and inline marks, select the matching block, and clear without losing formatting or pins.
Nested sections, inline code, tables, escaped markdown and Unicode retain correct offsets; comments, code fences and diagram labels do not match; query changes reuse the parsed AST.

sections.title: Curves
sections.summary: Specifies the curves that join the three panes for the current section: pure links and paths from measured rectangles, held inside their panes, measured by one Mount and lit along a chain on hover.

requirements.text: Curves are drawn for the current section only: one from its heading to each of its spec cards' headers, and one from each task row, a stray's too, to that task's chip.
`linksOf(cards)` is pure and returns those pairs as keys; each element a curve can end on carries its key in `data-wire`.
`wiresOf(links, boxes, panes)` is pure and returns, for each link with both ends measured, a Wire with its two keys, its path and `isOffPane`.
A curve runs from the middle of its source's right edge to the middle of its target's left edge; the PRD end leaves from the right edge of the PRD pane, level with the heading.
Each end's height is held inside its own pane, 8px in; a spec, row or chip end that had to be moved makes its curve `isOffPane`, and the PRD end does not count.
The path is a cubic bezier whose control points sit level with its ends, max(20, half the horizontal distance) in from each, computed by the reader itself.

A Mount on the reader body measures every `[data-wire]` element and the three panes at most once per animation frame, sends `MeasuredWires` only when a rectangle changed, and measures on mount, on a scroll in any pane, on a window resize, when a ResizeObserver on a pane or its content fires, and when `data-wires` changes.
`wiresView` is one fixed SVG over the reader body with no pointer events and `aria-hidden`; an `isOffPane` wire is dashed and fainter.
The PRD body and each card are lazy views, so a measurement renders the SVG again and nothing else.

A card's header, a task row and a chip send `HoveredNode` on pointer enter and focus and `LeftNode` on leave and blur; the hovered node's chain is drawn in ink and thicker, and every card, row and chip outside it is dimmed.

sections.title: Stacks
sections.summary: Lays the stacks pane out like the spec's stack diagram: one numbered box per stack, a chip per task bottom to top inside it, and the boxes in rows over the base branch by what they wait on, with the current section's tasks standing out.

requirements.text: `stacksOf(tasks)` is pure, replaces `stackLayoutOf`, and returns the stacks in number order, each with its number, root, area, level and cells.
A root is a task whose parent is null, names no task or would close a cycle; every other task belongs to its parent's stack, so each task is in exactly one stack.
Stacks are numbered from 1 in TaskIdOrder of their roots and labelled `Stack N · area`, the area being the second segment of the root's first spec section ID, or `Stack N` when it has none.
A task's row in its box is its depth along parent links, so a chain has no gaps; columns in a box follow the first-child-continues rule and are numbered by the ID of their first task.

A stack's level is 1 when it waits on no other stack, otherwise one more than the highest level among the stacks it waits on; a dependency that names no task or closes a cycle between stacks is ignored.

The view draws every stack whatever the current section is: the levels bottom to top, each a row of its stacks in number order aligned to the bottom, over a bar labelled with the base branch that is sticky at the bottom of the pane and is not a node; the pane starts scrolled to the bottom.
A stack is a box with `data-stack`, its number in a corner, `labelOf(stack)` as its title and aria-label, and a CSS grid of its cells, only as tall as its deepest chain.

A task is a chip: a button with `data-task` and `data-wire`, a status dot and the ID, a title and aria-label with the ID, title, branch, worktree and status, and a `--blocked` border when gated; it sends `ClickedTask`.
A chip in the current section's chain has `data-current`, an ink border and a hard shadow, and so does its box; every other chip is at 45% opacity and still takes focus, hover and clicks.
Over the diagram, sticky at the top: "N of M stacks hold this section · X of Y tasks done" and a legend.
Draw curves inside the pane: a chip sits on its parent, and the detail panel names a task's other dependencies.

decisions.why: Every stack in the bottom row starts from it, so curves to it would add nothing.

decisions.why: The rows already say what waits on what.

sections.title: Models and reasoning
sections.summary: Specifies how the reader shows the model and reasoning each task ran with, or the plan's choice when it has not run, and the switch that shows or hides them everywhere.

requirements.text: `ranOf(task)` returns the model and reasoning of the latest `running` event that carries both, with `ran: true`; otherwise the manifest's pair with `ran: false`, whatever the status.
A task row and the detail panel show a chip such as `sonnet · medium` on the model's colour.
A stack chip takes the model's colour and a mark after its ID: lo, med, hi, xhi or max.
A spec card's header has one small square per task in its model's colour.

Colours are the design system's `--m-opus`, `--m-sonnet` and `--m-haiku`, and `--m-other` for any other model, which is still named; a view sets `data-model` and the stylesheet gives the fill, with ink text on it.
What ran has a solid ink border; what is planned has a dashed one; each carries `data-ran` and a title that says which.
A "Models and reasoning" switch in the top bar, `switchView` with `role="switch"` and `aria-checked`, flips `isShowingModels`, which starts true.
With the switch off the views render no chip, mark or square, a done stack chip is filled green, and the legend's model entries are replaced by one for done.

sections.title: Panes
sections.summary: Specifies the dividers that resize the PRD pane, the spec pane and the detail panel by pointer or arrow keys, within limits, with the stacks pane taking what is left.

requirements.text: `Widths` is `{ prd, spec, stacks, detail }` in pixels, at first 520, 440, 480 and 600: what a person chose, not what the window has room for; until a person moves the stacks divider, the stacks pane takes its measured chart's width.
`resized(widths, pane, delta)` is pure and holds a width between its pane's limits: 300 to 3200 for the PRD, 260 to 3200 for the spec, 240 to 3200 for the stacks and 360 to 1800 for the detail panel.

The reader's grid, not the model, fits a window: its columns are prd, a divider, spec, a divider, stacks, its divider and minmax(320px, 1fr), so a window too narrow for the chosen widths scrolls the reader sideways and never narrows a pane, and the detail panel is never wider than the window.
A divider has `role="separator"`, a vertical orientation, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`, `tabindex="0"` and a label.

A primary press sends `PressedDivider`; while resizing, a subscription sends `MovedResizePointer` and `ReleasedResizePointer`, and a move sets the width to the width at the press plus the pointer's travel.
A move or release from another pointer is ignored, and a move with no button held ends a resize whose release was missed.
The detail panel's divider is on its left edge, so its delta is reversed.
With a divider focused, the left and right arrow keys send `PressedArrowOnDivider` and move it 24px.
The view writes the widths as CSS custom properties on the reader's grid, and the wires are measured again through their ResizeObserver.
Keep widths across reloads.

The wire carries a missing `reading` as null.
The viewer sends its current section when the socket opens and each time `currentOf` changes, a pin or an active search result included.
The room machine gains a `read` event, which sets that participant's `reading` and nothing else; an event for a participant not in the room is ignored.
`prdPaneView` shows each other participant's label as a chip beside the heading of the section they are reading; the top bar keeps "Here now".
`cursor`, the `Cursor` schema and the `moved` event are removed only with the canvas, behind its gate.

sections.title: Detail panel
sections.summary: Specifies the detail panel over the right of the reader: a trail of nodes, and for a task its status, what ran, its parent and dependencies, gate reasons, code, commits, traces and timeline.

requirements.text: The panel is fixed to the right edge of the reader, full height, with its own scroll and a divider on its left edge; it lies over the panes and does not move them.
The model holds `detail`, a trail of nodes; an empty trail is a closed panel and the last node is the one shown.

`ClickedTask` from a task row or a chip starts a new trail; `ClickedDetailNode` from inside the panel adds to it; `ClickedTrailStep` cuts it back to a step; `ClickedCloseDetail` empties it; `PressedEscape` removes the last step.
When the panel opens or its last node changes, focus moves to the panel's heading.

A task shows its ID, title, branch and stack; its status; `ranOf` as ran on or planned for; its parent or "from main"; each other task it depends on as a button that adds it to the trail; and its gate reasons.
Each commit is a button with its subject and short SHA that sends `ClickedOpenCode` with that commit, and "Open in code view" sends it with none.
Traces to: each PRD section as a button that sends `ClickedTraceSection` and scrolls the PRD pane to that heading, and each spec section as a button that adds it to the trail.
A task also shows the files the plan expects, its events timeline and its judgments.

A spec section shows its ID, summary, key chips, tasks as rows that add to the trail, and its judgments; each judgment shows its question, verdict, message and the probability or label and confidence behind it.
The path from a PRD section to a commit is two clicks: a task row of the current section, then a commit in the panel.

The reader's state and the detail panel's trail survive the code view, so Back to the plan returns the reader as it was; the tracking Mount scrolls the PRD pane to the current section when it mounts again.
"Open in code view" on a task in the detail panel opens its whole diff; a commit in the detail panel opens that commit.
The tree lists stacks in stackLayoutOf column order, tasks bottom up and commits oldest first; ClickedTreeTask selects a whole task, ClickedTreeCommit one commit and ClickedTreeFile a file.
Every tree row is a button and the selected row has aria-current.
A whole task fetches /api/diffs/:base/:head (head its newest commit, base the first parent of its oldest); one commit fetches /api/commits/:sha; either sends ReceivedPatch with the route path.
Patches and sessions are kept by route path and session ID, so returning to a selection draws it without a fetch; a failed fetch is retried on the next selection.

sections.title: Diff view
sections.summary: Renders a task's whole diff or one commit's diff with @pierre/diffs: parsePatchFiles into FileDiffMetadata, one vanilla CodeView in a Foldkit Mount, syntax-highlighted through the Highlights backend.

requirements.text: `ReceivedPatch` carries the patch text: `git show` output for one commit, `git diff` output for a whole task.
`parsePatchFiles` from `@pierre/diffs` turns the patch into `ParsedPatch`.
Cairn's code parse hunks itself; it reads the structure.
The selection renders through one vanilla `CodeView` inside a Foldkit `Mount`, one `diff` item per file with ID `diff:<path>` under a sticky path header.

The mount calls `setup` and `setItems`, watches `data-diff-style`, `data-file` and `data-turn` with a MutationObserver, and calls `cleanUp()` on unmount; the element is keyed by the patch's route path.
`diffStyle` is `unified`, with a toggle for `split`; the toggle is model state.
`lineDiffType` is `word-alt`, the default.
`hunkSeparators` is `line-info`, the default.
Light and dark follow `themeType: "system"`.

Code is syntax-highlighted with `preferredHighlighter: "highlights"` and `theme: { light: "pierre-light", dark: "pierre-dark" }`, the same lexers and light palette as fenced code; a language with no lexer is plain text and keeps its added and removed marks.
`diffOptionsOf(style)` in `diff.ts` is pure and gives the options the mount passes.
Files touched by a human-gated path are listed first, in the list and in the tree, with the matching pattern as a label.
Expanding context via `loadDiffFiles` and a route returning both versions of a file waits until someone asks.

sections.title: Resolving a link
sections.summary: Defines the pure `resolveLink` function that walks a deep link's steps against the trace and loaded data, returning the steps that open, the first step still waiting for data, and what is missing, plus the passage matcher, the finished-trunk rule, and the `linkNoticeView` status notice that tells the reader how far a link opened.

requirements.text: `resolveLink(trace, link, loaded)` in `links.ts` is pure, where `loaded` holds the patches and sessions the model has received.
`resolveLink` checks each step of the link in order and returns `resolved`, `waiting` and `missing`.
`resolved` lists the steps that open, each with what it needs: a passage step comes with its mark ranges and a diff step comes with its route path.
`waiting` is the index of the first step whose data is not loaded yet, or none.
`missing` holds what did not resolve; at most one miss stops resolution, and passage misses do not stop it.
A miss has the shape `{ index, step, reason, message }`.
A section step resolves when a section in `trace.prd` or `trace.spec` has its ID; otherwise it misses with `section-missing`, meaning the section was deleted.
A passage step resolves when its section resolves and the quote is found in it; otherwise it misses with `passage-changed`, which does not stop resolution, and the step opens as its section.
A task step resolves when `trace.tasks` has the task; otherwise it misses with `task-missing`.
A stack step resolves when `stacksOf(trace.tasks)` has a stack with that root; otherwise it misses with `stack-missing`.
A segment step resolves when that stack's finished trunk holds two or more tasks; otherwise it misses with `segment-missing`.
A diff step resolves when its `head` is one of the preceding task's commits; otherwise it misses with `commit-not-on-task`, meaning the branch was restacked or rewritten after the link was copied.
A commit step resolves when a task in the trace has the commit and, when a task precedes the step, that task is the preceding task; otherwise it misses with `commit-missing` or `commit-not-on-task`.

A file step resolves when the patch of the diff or commit before it is loaded and has the path; otherwise it misses with `patch-unavailable` (with the fetch error or the demo's missing patch) or `file-not-in-diff`.
A lines step resolves when the file's hunks show every line from `start` to `end` on that side; otherwise it misses with `lines-not-in-diff`.

A turn step resolves when a commit in the trace has the session, the session is loaded, and it has a turn with that ID; otherwise it misses with `session-missing`, `sessions-unavailable` in the demo, or `turn-missing`.
A note step never resolves yet and misses with `notes-unavailable`, because notes are not stored yet.
A step whose patch or session is not in `loaded` makes `waiting` that step's index, and resolution stops there until the data arrives.
`trunkOf(stack, tasks)` in `links.ts` defines the finished trunk: it starts at the root and takes the run of `done` or `landed` tasks up to the first fork or the first unfinished task.
A patch is turned into file names and hunk line ranges by the same patch-to-files step the diff view uses.
Link resolution must not parse a patch a second way, separate from the diff view's patch-to-files step.

`passageOf(index, section, quote)` finds a passage in the prose blocks its section owns, taking the blocks and their visible-text offset maps from the prose index, where nested sections own their own text.
For passage matching, the blocks' visible texts are joined with one space and whitespace runs are collapsed to one space.
The first exact, case-sensitive match of the quote counts as the passage.
A passage match is mapped back to a range in each block it covers.
An edit anywhere else in the document leaves a passage's ranges pointing at the same text, and an edit inside the passage removes the match.
`linkNoticeView` sits under the top bar of the reader and of the code view, with `role="status"`.
The link notice says how far the link opened and what is missing, for example: "Opened as far as task t74. `packages/cli/src/api.ts` is not in that diff."
A passage miss notice reads: "The passage changed: "…first 80 characters…" is no longer in Viewer."
A link that does not decode opens nothing and the notice shows its `LinkError`, for example: "This address is not a Cairn link: step 3 (file) must follow a diff or a commit."
The notice has a "Dismiss" button that sends `ClickedDismissLinkNotice`.
The next link that opens replaces the current notice.
The window must never be blank: at worst it shows the reader with no steps, under the notice.

sections.title: Opening a link
sections.summary: Makes the viewer a Foldkit application that owns the URL: it defines the viewer's only route, `linkRoute`, and `linkOf(model)`, which gives the canonical link of what is on screen. It also defines `openLink`, which applies a link step by step and fetches missing patches and sessions, and `withAddress`, which writes one browser history entry per step so Back walks the trail.

requirements.text: The viewer must become a Foldkit application that owns the URL.
`route.ts` must define `linkRoute` over `LinkFromPath` as the viewer's only route.
The implementer must read Foldkit's route and navigation declarations before writing `linkRoute`.

If Foldkit's route combinators can express a list of steps that print and parse from one definition, `linkRoute` must be built from them, with each argument's schema taken from the contract. Otherwise `linkRoute` must be one wildcard path run through `LinkFromPath`, and that Schema stays the single definition.
URL changes must arrive in the viewer as the `ChangedUrl` message.
`pushUrl` and `replaceUrl` must be commands.
A link must not carry a host, so that it opens the same way under `pnpm dev`, under `cairn serve` and on the demo site.
`pnpm dev` (Vite), `cairn serve` (through its `GET /*`) and the demo site must each answer any path that is not a file with the viewer's page.

The model must gain `reader.maybePassage` (the open passage's section and quote), `reader.maybeFocus` (a `stack` or `segment` and its root), `maybeLines` on the `Code` screen, `maybeHead` on `WholeTask`, `maybeLinkNotice`, and `maybePendingLink` (a link waiting for the first trace or for its data).
When `maybeHead` on `WholeTask` is None, the code view must show the task's newest commit, as before.

`linkOf(model)` in `links.ts` must be pure and must give the canonical link of what was opened, in this order: the pinned PRD section or a PRD passage in its place; a spec passage; the focused stack or segment; the detail trail's steps, each a `section` for a spec section or a `task`; a `task` step for the code view's task when that task is not the trail's last step; a `diff` with the head it shows, or a `commit`; the selected file, then `lines`; the highlighted turn.
A link must not hold the section at the top of the PRD pane, pane widths, the models switch, card density, cards opened by their header, or the search. Each viewer keeps those.
`openLink(model, link)` must resolve the link and clear what a link holds: the pin, the passage, the focus, the trail and the code view selection.
`openLink` must then apply each resolved step the way the click it stands for does.
A PRD section step must pin that section.
A spec section step must start the detail trail on the section, or add it to the trail when the panel is open.
A PRD passage step must pin the passage's section and mark the passage.

A spec passage step must pin the first PRD section the spec section implements when the pinned section is not one it implements. It must then open the spec section's card in `opened` and mark the passage.
A spec passage in a spec section that implements no PRD section must open in the detail panel, as search does.
A task step must start or extend the detail trail.
A stack or segment step must set the focus. The focused box gets `data-linked` and an ink outline, and for a segment its trunk's chips get them too.
A diff step must open the code view on the trail's last task at `head`.
A commit step must open the code view on that commit. When the trail's last task is a different one, the commit's task is first added to the trail.
A file step must select the file in the code view.
A lines step must set `maybeLines`.
A turn step must open the code view on the session's newest commit when no code step came before it, then highlight the turn as `ClickedTurn` does.
Passage marks must be `mark[data-link-passage]` nodes, placed by the same range splitting that search marks use.
Passage marks must have an ink underline and no fill, so a search mark inside one still shows.
The diff mount must gain a `data-lines` attribute, such as `n40-42`. Its `MutationObserver` reads the attribute to scroll to those lines and select them.
Line selection must use `@pierre/diffs`' line selection if `CodeView`'s declarations have one. Otherwise it must draw a line annotation, as the turn marks do.

For each step past the longest prefix the old link and the new link share, `openLink` must return a scroll command that brings the step into view, whether it is a heading, a passage's first mark, a card, a chip or a box.

For each patch or session the steps need that is not loaded, `openLink` must return a fetch command through the requests the code view already makes, so a link opened in a new window loads its diff and its turn.

When `ReceivedPatch` or `ReceivedSession` arrives for `maybePendingLink`, the link must be resolved again. A step that is now missing is taken out of the state, its notice is shown, and the address is replaced with `replaceUrl(linkOf(model))`.
A path that fails `LinkFromPath` decoding with a `LinkError`, or a step that `resolveLink` cannot find in the trace, must show the link notice.
`withAddress(update)` must wrap the viewer's update.

On first load, `init` must decode the URL into `maybePendingLink`, and the first trace must open it. History is then rewritten with one entry per step: `replaceUrl` with the first step, then `pushUrl` for each longer prefix.
A `ChangedUrl` from Back, Forward or a typed address must open that link without writing history.
A `ChangedUrl` whose link equals `linkOf(model)` must do nothing, which also absorbs the echo of the viewer's own `pushUrl`.

After any other message, if `linkOf` changed, the new link must be pushed. Each of these becomes one history entry, so Back undoes them one step at a time: pinning, opening a task or a spec section, cutting or shortening the trail, Escape, opening the code view, selecting in its tree, selecting lines, highlighting a turn, and "Back to the plan".
Escape with the detail panel closed must also clear the focus, as it unpins.

sections.title: Copying a link
sections.summary: Adds copy-link buttons across the viewer (PRD headings, spec cards, passages, the detail trail, stack boxes, the code view, diff lines and session turns). The buttons copy the same deep link the address bar holds, or a shorter link that opens one step on its own. The section also defines the pure `aloneOf` function in `links.ts`, which builds that shortest link.

requirements.text: Copying the address bar must copy the deep link. The copy-link buttons must give the same link text without navigating to it.
`aloneOf(link, index)` in `links.ts` must be pure. It must return the shortest link that opens the given step by itself.
For `aloneOf`, a section, passage, task, stack, segment, commit, turn or note step must be its own step, so the link holds only that step.
For `aloneOf`, a diff step alone must be its task plus the diff.
For `aloneOf`, a file step alone must be the diff or commit before it plus the file. For a diff, the diff's task comes first.
For `aloneOf`, a lines step alone must be the steps that the file needs, then the file, then the lines.
`copyLinkView({ path, label }, h)` must render a small `btn`. Clicking it must send `ClickedCopyLink` with the path.
On `ClickedCopyLink`, the update must run a Command that writes `location.origin` plus the path to the clipboard and then sends `CompletedCopyLink`.
After `CompletedCopyLink`, the copy-link button must read "copied" until the next render, as the section ID button does.
A PRD heading must have a "Copy link" button beside its section ID button that copies `/section/<id>` alone.
The pinned PRD section's status line row must copy the link up to that section's step.
A spec card header must have a "Copy link" button that copies the section alone.
The `TrackSelection` subscription in `subscription/selection.ts` must listen to `selectionchange` and handle it at most once per animation frame.
When both ends of the selection lie in one `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `SelectedPassage` with the section and the quote.
A PRD section's prose wrapper must carry its section ID in `data-passage`. A spec card's full section body must too.
The passage quote must be the selection's text, trimmed, with whitespace collapsed.
When the selection leaves a `[data-passage]` element, `TrackSelection` must send `ClearedPassageSelection`.

While a passage is selected, the section's status line row (in the PRD) or the card header (in the spec) must show "Copy link to passage". Clicking it opens the passage as a step, which pins the section and marks the passage, and copies the link up to that step.
When the selected passage is over 500 characters, the "Copy link to passage" button must be disabled, with the title "Select at most 500 characters to link to them."
In the detail panel, each step of the trail must have a "Copy link" button that copies the path up to that step.
The detail panel's heading must copy its task or spec section alone.
In the stacks pane, each box must have a "Copy link" button in its corner that copies `/stack/<root>`.
A stack box whose finished trunk holds two or more tasks must also have "Copy link to finished trunk", which copies `/segment/<root>`.
The code view top bar must have "Copy link", which copies the whole path.
The code view top bar must have "Copy alone", which copies `aloneOf` its last step. That step is the lines when lines are selected, and otherwise the file, the diff or the commit.

The diff mount must turn a line selection into `SelectedDiffLines` with the side, start and end. It uses the line selection callback of `@pierre/diffs`, or a click listener on the line-number gutter if the library has no such callback.
A line selection must join the current link.
In the session pane, an opened turn must have "Copy link", which copies the path up to that turn.
A link to lines copied from a task's diff must carry the `diff` step's head: the commit the code view showed when the link was copied. The link then opens on the same code after more commits land.

sections.title: List items
sections.summary: Makes list items that carry an ID behave in the viewer like small sections inside their section. Each such item gets a coverage annotation and a copyable ID. Items can be hovered, pinned and linked from spec cards and task rows, and their coverage counts toward the section's own counts.

requirements.text: `renderMarkdown` strips a trailing `{#id}` or `{#}` from a list item.
A list item with an ID gets `data-item` and `data-wire="prd:<id>"`, and ends with the `itemAnnotation` hook.
An item's annotation is a native button showing a status dot followed by counts such as `1 spec · 2/7 tasks`, taken from `countsOf(trace, id)`.
An item that nothing maps to shows `nothing maps to this` in place of the counts.
An item's ID is a small button that shows on hover and on focus within the item, and copies the ID on click through `ClickedSectionId`.
`chainOf(trace, section)` includes the chains of the items under the section.
A heading's status line and its section's cards count the whole section, including its items.
`HoveredNode` on an item's annotation lights the item's chain: its cards, their task rows and its chips.
`linksOf` adds a curve from an item to each of its cards.
`ClickedItemAnnotation` pins the item in `maybePinned`.
`currentOf` returns a pinned item. The spec pane then shows only that item's cards, and the stacks light only its tasks.
Clicking a pinned item's annotation again unpins it, and so does pressing Escape when no panel is open.
A card's `Implements` chips that name a PRD section or item are buttons that send `ClickedImplementsChip`.
`ClickedImplementsChip` scrolls the PRD pane to the item or heading and sets `reader.maybeMarked`. The element then has `data-marked` until the next click or hover elsewhere.
Hovering a task row or a chip gives `data-marked` to the items it builds.
The detail panel's "Traces to" list shows each of the task's items with the title of the section it is in, e.g. `prd.cli.lint · in CLI`.

sections.title: Cost on the graph
sections.summary: Builds the viewer's cost display: a pure `cost.ts` that labels, sums and attributes API-equivalent estimates and allowance use, and views that show cost in the task detail panel, on task rows and in card headers, including at narrow widths.

requirements.text: `cost.ts` is pure.
`compactOf(usage)` returns a short label of the form `API est. $0.42` when the estimate is complete.
`compactOf(usage)` returns a label of the form `API est. $0.42 · partial` when the estimate is partial.
`compactOf(usage)` returns `Usage unavailable` when there is no usage or no priced call.
`compactOf(usage)` never returns a `$0` label.
`cardCostOf(tasks)` sums share × estimate over distinct `(session, task)` pairs.
In `cardCostOf`, a session referenced twice is counted once, and a shared session counts only its share.
`cardCostOf` states its coverage in the form `1 of 2 tasks priced`.
`allowanceOf(tasks)` sums attributable percents only within the same allowance and `resetsAt`, and keeps each allowance's label.
The detail panel has a `Usage and cost` block placed below model and reasoning and before the commits and code.
The `Usage and cost` block's summary line shows the API-equivalent estimate and the attributable allowance consumed.

Expanding the `Usage and cost` block (via `disclosureView`) lists each session with its purpose and share, the actual models and reasoning per session, token categories, billed cost when known, allocated subscription cost when configured, and each rate's source and date, the assumptions and exclusions, and the coverage.
Account-wide allowance in the detail panel sits under its own `Account (all use)` label.
Account-wide allowance is never added to the task's cost or allowance.
On a task row, the `compactOf` label follows the model chip as a button that sends `ClickedCostEstimate`, which opens the task's detail with the cost block expanded.
The detail state's `isCostOpen` holds whether the cost block is expanded.
Selecting the task's chip opens the same task detail.
The card header shows the `cardCostOf` total, with its coverage when the total is partial.
The card header has a disclosure listing the contributing tasks and sessions.
The spec pane never adds card totals together.
Percentages always carry their allowance's label, such as `3% of codex-pro weekly`.
Task rows are a size container.
Below 380px row width, the cost moves to a second line under the title, while the title, model and status stay.
Every cost label is visible text and every detail is reachable through a button or a disclosure, so nothing depends on hover.

sections.title: What depends on what
sections.summary: Adds dependency links to the viewer: each heading and item shows how many sections it needs and how many need it, plus how many of its tasks are ready. A links button opens a list under the heading of what it needs, what needs it, and its next tasks. The task detail panel gains a `Needed by` list and says whether a pending task can start.

requirements.text: The reader must get section links by calling `sectionLinksOf` on the index it builds from the trace.
A heading's status line and an item's annotation must end with the counts of what it needs and what needs it, in the form `needs 3 · needed by 1`.
A section with unfinished tasks must add the number of tasks ready to start, such as `2 ready`, or `waiting` when none can start.
The links part of the status line or annotation must be its own button, sending `ClickedLinks`, separate from the pin button.
`reader.maybeLinksOpen` must hold the one section whose links list is open.
Clicking the links button of the open section again must close its links list.
Escape must close the open links list. It does so after an open panel has gone back and before a pin is cleared.
Opening a links list must not pin the section.
`linksView` must sit under the heading and show three groups: `Needs`, `Needed by` and `Next`.
The `Needs` group must list each section or item that is needed, with its status dot and the task pairs that link them, such as `t95 needs t94`.
The `Needed by` group must list each section or item that needs this one, with its status dot and the task pairs, the same way as `Needs`.
The `Next` group must list the section's unfinished tasks in build order with ready tasks first. Each task that is not ready shows what it waits on, such as `waits on t94`.
Clicking a section or item entry in the links list must send `ClickedLinkedSection`, which scrolls the PRD to that section or item and marks it.
Clicking a task entry in the links list must send `ClickedTask`.
Hovering an entry in the links list must send `HoveredNode` for that entry, which lights its tasks in the stacks.
A `switchView` labelled "Everything before and after" must set `reader.isLinksTransitive`. When it is set, the links lists show the transitive dependencies in build order.
The task detail panel must list `Needed by` beside the task's parent and dependencies.
For a pending task, the task detail panel must say `Can start now`, or `Waits on` followed by the tasks it waits on, such as `Waits on t94, t95`.

sections.title: Command menu
sections.summary: Builds a ⌘K-style command menu for the viewer in Foldkit: a modal dialog opened by ⌘K/Ctrl+K, `/` or the toolbar search button. It lists commands, tasks, and PRD and spec matches ranked by the same fuzzy search index as the toolbar search. It also has nested search pages, keyboard navigation, chain preview and an accessible combobox/listbox view.

requirements.text: The command menu must rank results with the fuzzy search index, so that the menu and the toolbar search box never disagree.
`menuKeys.ts` must listen to `keydown` events on the document.
⌘K on macOS, or Ctrl+K on other platforms, must send `PressedMenuShortcut`, which opens the menu when closed and closes it when open.
The platform must be read once, from `navigator.userAgentData` or `navigator.platform`.
Typing `/` must send `PressedMenuShortcut` only when the event's target is not an input, a textarea or editable content.
The toolbar search box must become a button showing the current query, and a click on it must open the menu.
Opening the menu must store the focused element's ID in `returnFocus`, and closing the menu must focus that element again.
`menuResultsOf(model)` in `menu.ts` must be a pure function.
With an empty query on the root page, `menuResultsOf` must list the commands, then the current section's tasks.
With a non-empty query, `menuResultsOf` must run the fuzzy search and group the results under PRD, Spec, Tasks, then Commands, in that order.
A result group with no matches must be hidden.
On a nested page (tasks, prd or spec), only results of that page's kind must be listed.
Each menu result must carry its kind, its title and its matched ranges, and a task result must also carry its status and ID.

The menu's commands must be the viewer's existing controls: toggling models and reasoning on or off; choosing Titles, Summary or Full spec for the cards; opening the code view; copying a link to what is in view; and `Search tasks…`, `Search the PRD…` and `Search the spec…`, which open a nested page.
The open-the-code-view command must apply only when the detail panel shows a task.
The copy-link command must copy a link to what is in view by sending `ClickedCopyLink` with `linkOf(model)`.
The fold/unfold-every-finished-trunk command must not be listed until the stacks pane folds trunks. After that it must be listed.
Each command must have an `appliesTo(model)` predicate, and a command that does not apply must not be listed.
A command that has a keyboard shortcut must show the shortcut on the right of its row.
Up and Down must move `active` through the results and wrap at the ends.
Pointer movement over a result must set `active` to that result.
The active search result must preview its chain behind the menu, as the active fuzzy search result does: `currentOf` takes the menu's active result while the menu is open.
Enter, or a click on a result, must run the active result.
Running a search result must close the menu and set the search query and the active search result to it, exactly as selecting it in fuzzy search does.
Running a command must close the menu and run the command.
On a nested page, Backspace on an empty query, or Escape, must go back to the root page.
Escape on the root page must close the menu and discard the preview. The panes, the pin and the detail panel must return to how they were before the menu opened.
After a search result has run from the menu, a second Escape must clear the search, as it already does.
`PressedEscape` must reach the detail panel only when the menu is closed.
`menuView` must render a `role="dialog"` element with `aria-modal="true"`, placed over the centre of the window.
The menu's query input must have `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` and `aria-activedescendant`.
On a nested page, the menu must show that page's badge before the query input.
Results must be a `role="listbox"` with `role="group"` sections labelled by their headings, and `role="option"` items with `aria-selected`.
Tab and Shift+Tab must keep focus on the query input while the dialog is open.
The result list's height must follow the number of its results.
The dialog must fade and scale in over `--d-fade`, and with reduced motion `base.css` must turn that animation off.
A query with no matches must show the message `No matches for "<query>"`.

sections.title: Notes
sections.summary: Builds the viewer's read-only display of notes: a pure `notesOf` that resolves each note's anchor and places it beside a heading or passage, on a spec card header, on a task row and chip, or on a diff line, or lists it as missing. It also covers the views for markers, counts, diff annotations, the task detail list and a switch that shows resolved notes.

requirements.text: The viewer must not let people write notes; it only shows them.
`notesOf(trace, loaded, isShowingResolved)` in `notes.ts` is pure.
`notesOf` decodes each note's anchor with `LinkFromPath` and resolves it with `resolveLink`, then places the note by the last step that resolved.
A note whose last resolved step is a passage or a PRD section shows beside the heading or the passage.
A note whose last resolved step is a spec section shows beside the card's header.
A note whose last resolved step is a task or a commit shows on the task's row and chip.
A note whose last resolved step is lines in a diff shows on that line in the diff.
A note whose anchor does not resolve all the way is listed in the task detail when its link names a task, and under its section otherwise.
A note whose anchor does not resolve all the way carries the missing step's message, as defined in `spec.viewer.deep-links.resolving-a-link`.
A note marker is a small button showing the count of open notes.
Opening a note marker shows each note's kind, author, status and markdown body rendered through `renderMarkdown`, with a link that opens the note's anchor.
Task rows and chips show `◆` followed by the number of open notes, such as `◆ 2`.
In the diff, notes on lines go into the mount's `data-notes` attribute as JSON, which the mount's `MutationObserver` reads and draws as line annotations, the same way turn marks are drawn.
The task detail lists the task's notes, and each one opens its link.
Resolved notes are hidden unless `isShowingResolved` is on.
A `switchView` labelled "Show resolved notes" sets `isShowingResolved`, which is local to the window.

tests.text: Every note is placed exactly once, either at its anchor or in a missing list.
A resolved note is hidden unless the "Show resolved notes" switch is on.
With a review on a diff line, the note is found in the mount's `data-notes` and in the task detail, and opening its link reaches that line.
A note on a deleted section shows under the task with its missing step.

decisions.text: The viewer only shows notes. Letting people write notes in the room is left to v2.
Resolved notes are hidden by default and shown only through a switch. The switch's state, `isShowingResolved`, is local to the window.
Diff line notes reach the diff through the mount's `data-notes` JSON attribute and its `MutationObserver`, the same mechanism that draws turn marks.

sections.title: Testing
sections.summary: Groups the model-based tests: the tools, then one model per piece of code tested against it.

sections.title: Model-based tests
sections.summary: Adds @xstate/test on xstate 6.0.0-beta.5 and sets how a model test is written, seeded, covered and replayed.

requirements.text: The catalog moves `xstate` to `6.0.0-beta.5` and adds `@xstate/test` `2.0.0-beta.3` and `fast-check` `4.11.0`; `core`, `cli` and `viewer` take them as dev dependencies, and `viewer` takes `xstate`.
The xstate docs index is regenerated and `AGENTS.md` gains a lookup row for model-based testing.
A model test lives in `<subject>.model.test.ts`, and its model is a machine that is never the code under test; when the code runs that machine, the test is of what the code adds around it.
A model test runs `propertyTest` in `it.effect` with a fixed seed and asserts `{ transitions: 1 }` coverage.
Events come from the model's schemas through `eventsFromSchemas` from `@xstate/test/effect-schema`, with an `override` for `Option`.
A failure's fixture is committed and replayed with `replayTest` and `expect: "pass"`; no test passes `failures: true`.
Each task breaks its code once and shows the test fail with a shrunk sequence.

sections.title: Presence against the room machine
sections.summary: Tests the presence server over real WebSockets against the room machine, so every participant sees the machine's room.

requirements.text: The server runs `roomMachine`, so the test is of what it adds: the sockets, the broadcast to every participant and leaving when a socket closes.
The model is `roomMachine` and the system under test is `PresenceRoute` with `Room.layer` on a Node server on port 0, with real WebSocket clients.
Model IDs come from a pool of three and map to the client and server ID each joined with.
`joined` opens a client, replacing an existing one; `moved` writes a `CursorJson` frame; `left` closes the client; an event for an ID with no client does nothing.

`read` waits until every open client has the room after the last event, up to two seconds, and returns each client's room with IDs mapped back; `projectModel` returns the machine's participants once per open client.

tests.text: Every participant sees the room machine's participants, in order, after every generated join, move and leave.
Sending the room only to the participant who changed it fails the test.

decisions.text: Test the server against the machine it runs.
decisions.why: The machine's transitions have their own tests; this one checks the sockets and the broadcast the server adds.

sections.title: Reader interactions against models
sections.summary: Tests the viewer's update against two machines written from the spec: the detail trail with pinning and Escape, and the pane dividers.

requirements.text: The models are written from the spec sections, not from the viewer's code, and the system under test is `update` from `init` on the demo trace with the reader open.
The reader model covers starting, extending, cutting and closing the trail, Escape that steps back or unpins, and pinning by the status line.
The panes model covers arrow keys, a press, moves and releases from the pressed pointer and from another, and a move with no button held, within limits written out in the model.
Payloads come from the demo trace's IDs, and a step index from the current trail.

sections.title: Derivation against a model of its inputs
sections.summary: Tests derive against a machine of what an orchestrator writes and what git shows, which keeps facts and replays them as derive recomputes.

requirements.text: The model is a machine of one task's inputs, written from the PRD, and not the task machine.
The model keeps facts: the reports so far, whether a commit touched a gated path and whether the task landed; after each event it replays its reports from the start and carries nothing over.
`reported` lines follow the lifecycle, a gated `done` waits for a human, and a report the lifecycle does not allow adds a warning.

`committed` on a gated path gates every report of the task, earlier ones too; `merged` and `squashed` stay true and land the task from any status, with a warning for landing without approval when it is gated and its reports do not end in `done`.
`read` runs `derive` with a test `Git` Layer over shuffled event lines and returns the status and the number of warnings.

tests.text: derive agrees with the model on status and warnings after every generated report, commit and landing, whatever the order of the lines.
Letting an agent's done approve a gated task fails the test.

decisions.text: Replay the facts in the model instead of keeping a running status.
decisions.why: derive computes the gate from every commit before it replays events, and landing is git state that stays true.

sections.title: Acceptance
sections.summary: Maps each PRD acceptance criterion to how it is checked.

requirements.text: Check three or more stacked tasks on a RinkSide feature with a dogfood run, keeping `cairn status` output with the feature.
`cairn status` warns on a commit without trailers or with a session missing from `cairn.db`.
No child leaves `pending` before a human approves its gated parent.
Correct status and two clicks to commits are checked by rollup property tests and a Scene test that clicks a section and then a commit.
Lint catches orphaned and unmapped sections, tested for `unknown-section` and `unmapped-section`.
An oversized draft is broken down before printing, checked by a refine test whose plan output lists the split.
A model changes only when Jev is confident, checked by a routeOf property test and a refine test.
A changed task's judgment shows stale, checked by a trace test.
Fuzzy search finds and highlights matching text and its chain; matching properties and Scene tests cover navigation, markdown spans, refresh and preserving the pin on clear.
Scrolling the PRD changes the cards and the lit stacks, checked by `sectionAtTop` properties and a Scene that sends `ScrolledPrd`; a pinned section holds.
Models and reasoning show what ran or what is planned, checked by `ranOf` properties and a Scene that finds `data-ran` on rows and chips and none of them with the switch off.
A task's code shows in the detail panel, checked by a Scene that clicks a task row and finds the diff mount keyed by the task's range with the reader still under it.
A broken broadcast or Escape fails a model-based test that prints the shortest failing event sequence.
